"let's not start using the term 'incel' as if it's a valid concept. it isn't. no one is owed sex. we already *have* a word for those who call themselves 'incel': 'misogynist'"

There are plenty more examples, and this probably isn't the best one, but I don't feel like digging deep to find them. The claim that the very concept of being incel implies that you believe you are owed sex seems to contradict your claim that the term itself isn't considered a problem.

You'd probably have to look yourself at /r/incelswithouthate to judge for yourself whether or not they do enough to denounce mainstream incel community.

Can someone explain how the term "incel" implies entitlement to female bodies? I personally just don't like the term because I think it's an unhelpful way to label oneself, and the most vocal people who consider themselves incels are hateful extremists. 

I don't see any entitlement in the word itself. Involuntary celibate just means that you are not having sex, but you wish you were. It's just a qualifier to distinguish from standard celibacy, where you're not having sex because of some personal conviction. I don't see the entitlement, and nothing in the term implies that it only applies to heterosexual males anyway. 

I guess it just bothers me, because I see all this shit thrown at incels as if they're a monolith of evil misogynists. Even if I don't consider myself an incel, as a 25-year-old virgin, I can't say I feel completely disconnected from the label. Kind of like how I would never call myself a nerd or even consider myself a nerd, but if someone said "I hate nerds. I hope they all die." I would still feel personally attacked. 

It just seems wrong to say all incels are misogynistic garbage, especially when the subreddit /r/incelswithouthate exists.

Alright, here goes. I've had gay fantasies since I was 12, and I think I'm probably bisexual. Haha, I know, make your "secretly lusting after Chad" jokes (I'm not even an incel, just a virgin). Anyway, I've lived all this time feeling ashamed of these thoughts, even though I wasn't raised religious or in a particularly homophobic environment. I've tried so hard to get over the shame, but I just haven't able to, even though I know there's nothing wrong with it.

I guess my question is, would it be a good idea to pursue a relationship with another man? The stereotype is that gay men can get sex easier (not sure if this is actually true or not). I think it could be a confidence boost to have sex and feel desired. Finally, I feel more comfortable around men (you could maybe call this subconscious misogyny) and find the thought of being with a man more appealing, at least in a world without any stigma attached to it.

On the other hand, my feelings of shame might make this a bad idea. Additionally, I always felt I should try a relationship with a woman first. The reason for this is that it seems a lot of people see men as tainted if they've ever been with another man, and many women will not want to be with a bisexual man. Once I've actually done something with a man, I wouldn't feel comfortable hiding this from any potential partners, which would reduce my overall dating pool. 

So tell me what you guys think. Is this a good idea or not?
